values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (eShopModernizedNTier\src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-70) reads the shared database MAX(Id), increments it locally, then saves an inserted row without synchronization covering that read/write sequence. CatalogItem explicitly disables database-generated identifiers (eShopModernizedNTier\src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:13-15). The basicHttpBinding service endpoint (eShopModernizedNTier\src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:37-40) can serve concurrent independent request instances; per-instance WCF serialization does not serialize their shared database. Two requests can read the same maximum and insert the same new primary key, causing a failed request. SaveChanges atomicity does not include the earlier MAX query. This single race is mapped to the applicable shared-data/synchronization rules, not separate independent incidents.

result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 3 FOUND, 3 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed all handwritten source for singleton ownership, shared mutable state, locking, WCF instance behavior and EF transaction boundaries. Confirmed one database ID-allocation race mapped to three applicable rules. No active singleton misuse, erroneous explicit lock protocol or attempted-but-incorrect synchronization was confirmed. Static interleaving analysis only; no concurrent runtime test. Generated/test/temp/dependency code excluded.
